authorization.source: explicit human instruction in the active pi session
authorization.scope: post-hoc exploration of the two-tolerance hypothesis using native Wannier/Wigner-Seitz shell truncations; no Slater-Koster model

hypothesis.tau_1: uniform-408-point RMS ordered-spectrum error divided by 1 eV
hypothesis.tau_2: uniform-408-point RMS Hamiltonian Frobenius error per retained state divided by 1 eV
hypothesis.question: for each threshold pair, does at least one proper reduced native Wigner-Seitz shell candidate satisfy both inequalities?
hypothesis.status: post-hoc descriptive exploration; thresholds are not prospective acceptance limits

candidate_family.source: authenticated full untruncated C6-B20-W21 rank-10 Wannier Hamiltonian
candidate_family.alignment: identity; no fitted global or pointwise gauge action
candidate_family.shells: H-shell-00 through H-shell-16 are proper reduced candidates
candidate_family.full_support_control: H-shell-17 is reported at (0,0) but excluded from reduced-family feasibility because it would make every nonnegative threshold pair trivial
candidate_family.mask: retain every effective Wigner-Seitz representative in each complete physical-radius shell

additional_maps: maximum ordered-spectrum error versus maximum per-state Frobenius error
minimum retained support over the complete tau_1-tau_2 plane
